Fix: rename the product-catalog Service port to use a protocol-prefixed name (e.g., 'http', 'http2' or 'grpc') or explicitly configure Envoy upstream protocol.

final_report.root_cause: Misconfigured product-catalog Service port name caused Envoy (frontend-proxy) to infer the wrong upstream protocol (treated as raw TCP rather than HTTP/gRPC). That protocol inference/mismatch led to gRPC/HTTP semantics being mishandled and produced the observed "13 INTERNAL: Error: Product Catalog Fail" responses. A secondary, unrelated observability failure (the OpenTelemetry exporter in the product-catalog pod reporting "exporter export timeout: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = data refused due to high memory usage") was present in pod logs and caused noisy telemetry errors but did not cause the user-facing product lookup failures.
affected_resources: telemetry backend / OTEL collector (ingester) - observed memory pressure (rejected exporter data)
final_report.evidence_summary: Key evidence: (1) 20 traces showing product-catalog spans returning "13 INTERNAL: Error: Product Catalog Fail", with failures observed by frontend-proxy. (2) product-catalog Service port is named 'tcp-service' (8080) — not protocol-prefixed — while Envoy relies on service port naming to infer upstream protocol (http/grpc/http2). (3) product-catalog and astronomy-db pods are Running and product-catalog logs show no DB errors or application stack traces, ruling out DB connectivity/application crashes. (4) product-catalog pod logs contain repeated OpenTelemetry exporter timeouts: "exporter export timeout: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = data refused due to high memory usage", indicating the telemetry backend is under memory pressure and rejecting data (observability issue). (5) frontend-proxy/Envoy logs show normal startup but do not contradict the protocol inference issue; Envoy may not log a clear error for protocol-mis-inference at the retrieved log level.
